member: Lena — Refrigeration and Thermal Insulation Engineer
message:
Surya, Farah, Kofi, the cold box holds one tonne with low leak using the 100 mm Polyurethane sandwich-panel cold box (C4), where Polyurethane (PU) means rigid foam insulation. A bedroom-size box with thick foam lets in only a few hundred watts in hot sun. Numbers are 2.00 by 2.00 by 2.20 m inside, area 25.6 square metres, conductivity 0.022 W per m K with 100 mm thickness per panel data (E14), giving 0.22 W per square metre K and 186 W for 33 K lift, sane against a household freezer scaled to a room.

Cooling comes from the Direct Current vapor-compression chiller (C5), where Direct Current (DC) means battery power and Coefficient of Performance (COP) means cooling per electric watt. A small solar fridge compressor running steadily holds 4 to 10 C. Numbers are COP 2.90 to 3.10 per compressor data (E20) and 100 to 300 W per unit per cooler data (E22), giving about 3.61 kWh per day electric for 376 W thermal.

Even air uses the uniform low-velocity airflow (C6). Loose crates and a fan prevent hot spots plus respiration and door air heat. Numbers are pull-down 25.0 kWh thermal per structure report (E19) and journal (E17), sane against one-third of a household day. Door openings and loading rate are unagreed, so not ready.
